question: When a motorcar makes a sharp turn at a high speed, we tend to get thrown to one side. This example is based on which law of motion?
solution:
The correct answer is __**First law of motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The tendency to get thrown to one side when a motorcar makes a sharp turn at high speed is explained by **Newton's First Law of Motion**.
 
• Newton's First Law of Motion states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• This law is also known as the law of inertia, where inertia is the resistance of any physical object to any change in its velocity.
 
• When the car turns, the passengers inside experience a force due to inertia that makes them feel as if they are being thrown outward.
 
• This outward force is actually the inertia of the passengers trying to keep them moving in a straight line while the car changes direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Second Law of Motion**

 
 
• This law states that the acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass.

• **Third Law of Motion**
 
 
• This law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• This means that forces always come in pairs; if one object exerts a force on another, the second object exerts a force of equal magnitude but in the opposite direction on the first object.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Momentum**
 
 
• This principle states that the total momentum of a closed system is conserved if no external forces are acting on it.
